setup.mode.description: This choice is locked once setup finishes.

setup.basics.app_url_hint: The address people use to reach this app, including https://.

setup.run.summary.title: What will be set up

setup.pizzasys.env.production_descriptio: The portal your team signs in with every day.
setup.pizzasys.env.testing_description: A second portal for trying changes safely. Leave it empty if you do not have one; you can add it later in Settings.
setup.pizzasys.label: Display name
setup.pizzasys.label_hint: Only used on this page. Optional.
setup.pizzasys.base_url_hint: The web address of the portal, for example https://auth.example.com. Plain http only works for localhost and .test hosts.

setup.pizzasys.token_keep_hint: Leave this empty to keep it, or paste a new one to replace it.

setup.pizzasys.roles.title: Who gets in
setup.pizzasys.roles.description: Which people are admins or agents is decided in the portal. Here you only say which permission names count.
setup.pizzasys.roles.admin_permission_hi: Anyone who has this permission in the portal is an administrator here.
setup.pizzasys.roles.agent_permission_hi: Anyone who has this permission can take chats.
setup.pizzasys.roles.super_roles_hint: Portal roles that always mean administrator, even without the permission above. Press Enter after each name.

setup.pizzasys.portal.title: Sign in as a portal admin
setup.pizzasys.portal.description: Prove the connection end to end with an Auth Portal account that has the :permission permission (or a super role). That account becomes this app's first administrator, and setup cannot finish without it.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: Categories are the topics visitors choose before chatting. They decide which agents receive a new chat.
categories.empty.title: No categories yet
categories.empty.body: Add topics such as Sales, Billing or Technical support. Each widget offers a chosen set of them.
categories.dialog.description: Visitors see the name; agents see it on every chat request.
categories.dialog.name: Name
categories.dialog.slug_hint: Used in embed settings such as data-categories. Lowercase letters, numbers and dashes. Leave it empty to generate it from the name.
categories.dialog.description_hint: Shown to agents when they choose the categories they serve.
categories.dialog.translations_hint: Optional. Visitors whose language matches see this name instead.
categories.dialog.active_hint: Inactive categories are hidden from visitors and receive no chats.
categories.validation.slug_format: Use lowercase letters, numbers and single dashes.
categories.validation.locale: Use a language code such as ar or pt-BR.
categories.delete.title: Delete :name?
categories.delete.body: It is served by :agents and offered in :widgets. Both lose it right away. This cannot be undone.
categories.delete.in_use_body: An active chat uses it right now, so it cannot be deleted yet. Deactivate it to stop new chats, then delete it once those chats end.

categories.support.description: Choose the categories you take chats for. You only receive requests for these.
categories.support.not_agent_title: Your account does not take chats
categories.support.not_agent_body: Only people who take chats choose the categories they serve. Switch on "Takes chats" for your account on the Agents page (or grant the agent permission in the Auth Portal), then come back here.
categories.support.empty_body: An administrator has to create and activate categories first.
categories.support.no_widgets: Not offered in any widget yet
categories.support.none_warning: You serve no category. Visitors are never offered to you, so no chat request will reach you until you pick at least one.
categories.support.saved: Saved. You now serve these categories.
categories.support.leave_confirm: You have unsaved changes. Leave this page without saving?
agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Everyone who can take chats. Assign the categories each person serves and how many chats they handle at once.
agents.stop.title: Stop :name taking chats?
agents.stop.body: This account serves :count of your support categories. They are removed, because only accounts that take chats can serve a category. If you turn "Takes chats" on again you have to pick the categories again.

agents.portal.body: Admin and agent access comes from the portal's roles and permissions, so activating, deactivating and role changes happen there. You can still assign categories and chat limits here.
agents.portal.body_generic: Roles and activation are managed outside this app. You can still assign categories and chat limits here.
agents.empty.title: No agents yet
agents.empty.body_manage: Add your first agent. They can sign in and start taking chats.
agents.empty.body_portal: Agents appear here after they sign in for the first time with a portal account that has agent access.

agents.create.role_hint: Staff accounts created here can take chats. Admin accounts are created during setup.
agents.create.role_agent_hint: Takes chats for the categories below
agents.create.categories_hint: Optional. Agents can adjust their own selection later.
agents.create.errors.name: Enter a name.

whatsapp.risk.body: This links an ordinary WhatsApp account through OpenWA, an unofficial gateway. WhatsApp does not allow automation, so the number can be restricted or banned at any time.

whatsapp.risk.inbound: Reply only to customers who wrote first, and keep that setting on.
whatsapp.risk.limits: Keep the sending limits below low: they are what protects the number.

whatsapp.connection.dirty_hint: Save your changes first: the test uses the saved address and key.
